label: GO after a rewarded visit to S1, late in the episode (strongest after rare a2->S1 reward)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps, only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=1 at D1), and only late in the episode (no activity before ep_trial ~55, rising sharply from trial 70, peak at 80-99; equivalently, when the value head is low, below ~7.1). Never fires at D1 or D2, and never after an unrewarded trial. Within that, it prefers trials whose previous visit reached S1 and was rewarded. The strongest and most selective case is a rare transition: a2 led to S1 and S1 paid out, the case where a model-based agent should switch to a1. Most top activations look like this, and model_act=a1 is enriched. Rewarded common S1 visits (a1->S1) also activate it, but more weakly, and they make up most of the missed mass. Rewarded S2 visits rarely activate it. The recorded predicate (rare-rewarded at S1, ep_trial>=70) has dev P=0.55, R=0.51, F1=0.53, mass recall 0.62. The broader version (any rewarded S1 visit, ep_trial>=70) has R=0.83 and mass recall 0.86 but P=0.16. A plain late-GO-after-reward predicate has mass recall 0.99 but P=0.08. The feature is sparse even inside the predicate, so precision stays incomplete. Every variable used is observed by the agent; the late-episode condition probably stands in for an internal clock or low value.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a2 S1 r, a1 S1 r, ?) and trial before (GO: a1 S1 u, a2 S2 u, a2 S1 u); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
